note: How big is the cold-zone prize, under each hypothesis about where the low-temperature leakage floor sits? Written 29 Aug 2026. This is the single number the architecture argument is most uncertain about -- ~50x -- and it needs no compute to bound.
why_it_matters_MORE_after_Test_1: Test 1 showed a monolithic die cannot hold a two-temperature gradient: 40 W of removal on a 60.7 W die buys 1.24 K against the 150 K asked for. That pushes the cold zone onto its own DIE -- and on a separate cache die you do not need a gradient at all, you cool the whole thing uniformly. So Test 1 does not kill the cold zone; it moves it somewhere the gradient problem does not exist, and makes the leakage-floor question the deciding number rather than a secondary one.

measured_baseline.source: McPAT block_powers_split, project trace (linpack, 7nm, T_ref 330 K)
measured_baseline.comment: the leakage is already concentrated in cache -- L3 alone is 89% of it

bounds.hypothesis: A: our calibrated curve, 350->310 K (all it can see)
bounds.note: the curve clamps below 310 K, so this is the whole defensible span
the book itself discounts this as unreachable

THE_SPREAD.reading: both hypotheses agree the prize is BOUNDED by the static fraction -- you cannot save more leakage than there is. The book's 100-200x and the ideal 2^15 differ by 3 orders of magnitude in reduction but only ~1% in die power saved, because both have already taken essentially all of it. The DECISION-RELEVANT gap is between our curve and the book: 13.5% against 31.7% of die power.

what_would_settle_it: PTM SPICE cards (ptm.asu.edu, free, 7nm among others) give leakage vs temperature over any range. McPAT cannot: it rejects input outside 300-400 K. One evening's work, and it converts the largest uncertainty in the architecture argument into a measured curve.
the_honest_position_today: our own calibrated curve supports a cold-zone prize of ~14% of die power, not the ~32% the book's numbers imply. Neither is authoritative -- ours is McPAT's model below its own calibration range, and the book's is a discounted textbook exponential. The disagreement should be stated, not resolved by picking the flattering one.
